The evidence suggests a pathway where Sebacaldehyde modulates the tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 10B, potentially influencing cellular signaling pathways critical for T-24 cell behavior. The integration of multiple targets and their downstream effects on T-24 cells indicates a plausible mechanism of action, though the exact molecular interactions remain to be fully elucidated. The observed scores reflect a consistent pattern of interaction, suggesting that Sebacaldehyde may act as a modulator of T-24 cell function through this pathway.
